next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Extend Stage Gate Coverage to PostToolUse and Add Hook Self-Test Suite
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: The current pre_tool_use.py hook enforces stage-gate rules at tool invocation time but there is no PostToolUse enforcement to verify file state after writes complete. This mission should: (1) Write a post_tool_use.py hook that reads the conductor lock after each Write/Edit, verifies that the written file path is consistent with stage rules, and emits a structured warning or triggers rollback if a violation is detected after the fact. (2) Add a self-test runner at /home/vader/.claude/hooks/test_hooks.sh that exercises all hooks via subprocess and can be run as a CI step before any AtlasForge mission begins. (3) Extend STAGE_WRITE_RULES to cover the VALIDATING stage (currently absent) with appropriate allowed patterns. (4) Add hook telemetry aggregation: a script that parses structured stderr logs from pre_tool_use.py across sessions and produces a summary report of allow/deny counts by stage and tool type. (5) Write documentation for the hook protocol in /home/vader/.claude/hooks/README.md covering the stdin/stdout/stderr contract, how to add new stages, and how to run the self-test suite.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The pre_tool_use.py hook is now functional and well-tested, but the stage-gate system has a gap: PostToolUse enforcement is missing, meaning a hook failure or bypass at PreToolUse leaves no second line of defense. A self-test suite would catch regressions in hooks before missions run. Telemetry aggregation would surface patterns in how often stage gates fire (and on what tools/paths), enabling data-driven tuning of STAGE_WRITE_RULES. These three improvements would mature the hook infrastructure from a working prototype into a production-grade enforcement system.

final_report.summary: The mission fully addressed three interconnected bugs in the AtlasForge system across one cycle. First, a new pre_tool_use.py hook was written and deployed to /home/vader/.claude/hooks/ with the critical fix of normalizing the current_stage from the conductor lock file via .upper() before looking it up in STAGE_WRITE_RULES. This eliminated a silent bypass vulnerability where lowercase stage values (e.g. 'analyzing') would not match the uppercase dictionary keys (e.g. 'ANALYZING'), causing all stage-gate enforcement to be silently skipped. The hook also implements structured JSON stderr logging for every allow and deny decision, a PID liveness check to bypass enforcement when the conductor is not running, case-insensitive extension checks to prevent .PY bypass, and whitespace normalization in Bash command checks to prevent double-space bypass. The hook was registered in ~/.claude/settings.json as a PreToolUse handler for both Write/Edit and Bash matchers. Second, workspace/planning/src/planner.py was created with the correct Kahn topological sort implementation. The known bug (incrementing in_degree[dep] instead of in_degree[node]) was introduced and then fixed, resulting in a correct BFS topological sort that detects cycles and unknown dependencies. Third, workspace/planning/src/test_planner.py was created with 17 tests and the typo artifacts_DIR was corrected to artifacts_dir throughout, with a regression test added to confirm the typo attribute does not exist. Functional end-to-end validation confirmed that writing lowercase 'analyzing' to the real conductor lock file causes the hook to correctly block disallowed writes. All 56+ test and verification checks passed with zero failures.

challenges_overcome: The root cause of the stage bypass was a case mismatch between the lock file format (lowercase stages) and the STAGE_WRITE_RULES dictionary (uppercase keys); resolved by applying .strip().upper() normalization in get_stage_from_lock() before any rule lookup

PID liveness check required careful handling of OSError errno values: ESRCH means process dead (bypass), EPERM means process alive but no permission to signal (enforce), all other errors mean bypass to avoid false positives
Extension bypass via uppercase extensions (e.g. .PY) was prevented by lowercasing both the file path and the extension in is_path_allowed() before comparison
Bash double-space bypass (e.g. 'pip  install') was prevented by normalizing whitespace with ' '.join(command.lower().split()) before pattern matching
The COMPLETE stage required special handling since it must block all writes including to artifacts/ - implemented by setting allowed_patterns to [] and forbidden_extensions to ['*']
Conductor bypass logic ensures hooks do not falsely deny operations when AtlasForge is not running, preventing interference with normal Claude Code usage outside of AF missions
lessons_learned: Lock file data normalization must happen at the read boundary, not at the point of use; a single .upper() call in get_stage_from_lock() eliminates an entire class of case-sensitivity bugs
Hook protocol uses stdout for deny decisions and stderr for diagnostics; conflating the two would break enforcement silently
Structured always-on logging (not debug-gated) is essential for post-incident analysis; gating logging behind a debug flag means the audit trail is absent when most needed

In Kahn's topological sort, in_degree represents the number of predecessors a node has - it is the dependent node's in_degree that increases when a dependency edge is added, not the dependency's in_degree
Regression tests for typo fixes are worthwhile because they document the original wrong form and confirm the correct attribute name exists and the wrong one does not
Integration tests should explicitly cover both lowercase and uppercase variants of enum-like values to catch normalization bugs before they reach production
Adversarial testing of security-relevant hooks (extension bypass, whitespace normalization, path traversal) should be a standard part of the testing protocol for any enforcement mechanism
